motivation: Strengthen the existing guide-validation question by estimating reproducibility of guide-specific responses conditional on product and cell. Do not reinterpret the uncertain balanced product-level correlation gap as significant.
prior_outcome_knowledge: All underlying guide outcomes and product averages were already analyzed in C87/88. This is a retrospective new estimand, not preregistration or independent data.
universe: 127 exact complete-reference coding-chain/DNA product matches. Both-source geometry and coverage eligibility inherited unchanged from C87; shared guides must map to identical chromosome and cut. No fresh-guide requirement.
primary_cohort: At least3 shared eligible guides, finite both-screen LFC in all3 common cells. Metadata preflight:105products/105clusters/471guide sequences. Do not relax threshold.
primary_endpoint: Equal-product and equal-cell weighted Pearson correlation between old and new guide LFC after subtracting each product-by-cell shared-guide mean in each screen. Each guide-cell weight=1/(3*nSharedGuidesAtProduct). This measures persistent relative guide response, not peptide causality.
uncertainty: 2000 dependence-cluster bootstrap draws, seed20261015,95%percentileCI. All guides and3cells per product move jointly. One primary endpoint.
permutation_check: 5000 within-product random guide-identity permutations; each guide permutation fixed jointly across3cells, seed20261016. Two-sided add-one empiricalP for primarycorrelation. This tests pairing association under exchangeability, not independent biological replication or off-target causation.
secondary: Within-product-by-cell guide ranks instead of rawLFC
Descriptive GC-by-cell adjustment of both centred responses
Raw covariance decomposition into between-product and within-product contributions after removing common cell means; no causal variance attribution
claim_limits: A persistent guide response could reflect on-target disruption efficacy, RNA/regulatory effects, off-target effects or other site/reagent properties.
Exact sequence reuse does not prove intentional design transfer.
Complete product identity is a reference-model comparison, not experimentally verified protein equivalence.
The balanced product-level agreement difference remains uncertain, irrespective of this residual result.
This analysis cannot establish a new medical target or clinical safety.
